detail: mdb cannot yet be pointed at mrun's native runtime (QStore + paged kernels): attach() refuses anything that is not a Hugging Face module tree, and the analysis verbs read weights from HF modules. It is feasible, measured two ways. (1) Tiny Qwen2 fp32 on CPU, lossless FP32 QStore: a proxy around the store (the kernel's only weight seam: embed_rows and matmul(name, x)) leaves paged_forward_kv bitwise unchanged, stops at any of the 43 seam points and re-enters bitwise, and gives 16 ports (h a q k v qr s p A o r n g u f m) bitwise equal to mdb's engine on Hugging Face, logits included; zeroing one MLP neuron changes the logits by the same bits in both. (2) Qwen2.5-1.5B, int8 QStore, CUDA: decode token 11.9 ms, 11.8 ms through an inert proxy, 12.7 ms capturing all seam values (393 seam calls); reaching a stop from the token boundary 0.2 ms (L0) to 10.2 ms (L27); stop and re-entry bitwise; rerun bitwise; the attention replica rebuilt from the seam and the K/V arena equals the observed o_proj input exactly; K/V cell edits are a direct arena write: base margin -4.8048, effects A 3.519 / B 0.812 / A+B 4.873, interaction 0.542 (mdb on HF with re-rounded int8 weights: -4.8047, 3.517 / 0.812 / 4.871, 0.542). Kernel-vs-HF port differences on the real model (up to 1.3e-3 relative, logits 0.066) come from the weights, not the arithmetic: the store's int8 weights differ from a torch re-rounding of the checkpoint in 11k-584k elements per matrix, while store.matmul equals F.linear on the store's own weight bitwise. The int8 store is a different model from the bf16 checkpoint (margin -4.80 against -4.75; effects 3.52 / 0.81 / 4.87 against 3.75 / 1.0 / 5.125); no FP32 store of this model exists on beast. Not tested: batched kernel (batched_paged_logits), the CUDA decode graph, dense-qstore-cuda (fused SwiGLU and residual-norm kernels hide n/g/u/f), MLX, ANE, MoE kernels. mrun's `hf` backend already works unchanged (job-6470ef881011; needs attn_implementation='eager' and a dtype in model_kwargs).

detail: `verify` confirms a forecast when the measured residual is within N dtype spacings at the consumer's magnitude. N = 2 for a scalar target, N = 4 for a margin or a vector port. A vector port's floor is taken at its largest element although elements round at their own magnitudes.

Spacing at each element's own magnitude is not usable (up to 1e4 own spacings on correct forecasts). `residual_spacings` is printed. detail: The M30 verify floor (3 x sqrt(n) x spacing at the result's magnitude) does not hold on the real model at shallow depth: forecast t21.L0.m sealed at t21.L0.h, 17 rounded identities, residual 0.378 = 48 spacings against a floor of 12.4 spacings, verdict `not confirmed`; residual/(sqrt(n) x spacing) = 11.7 against the supplied 3 (tiny-model maximum 2.18). Deeper targets pass with wide room (L10.m 7.2 of 43 spacings, L27.m 0.94 of 69, logits 1.6 of 69, margin 0.022 of 69). Not known which: (a) native bf16 accumulation over 1536- and 8960-term sums whose terms are much larger than the result (then the floor must scale with the sum of |terms|, which the chain can compute, not with the result's magnitude), or (b) a real error in the forecast chain at L0.m on CUDA. A residual of 0.378 on a vector whose max_abs is 1.79 is large. MEASURED 2026-11-13 (jobs job-382daba8d1f5, job-84918c75d24e, job-eee4ae968b0b; Qwen2.5-1.5B, HF eager, cuda RTX 4080, torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.13.1; one prompt, row t21): the forecast chain is correct (every stage recomputed in float64 from its native inputs is within 1.17 spacings). The 0.378 is native rounding of L0 attention scores (|s| about 1.3e4, bf16 spacing 64, exact-distinct sources rounded into ties) amplified by softmax (p error 0.49 in head 1), carried through A, o, n, g/u to m; down_proj accumulation is 0.44 spacings. A float64 chain that rounds to bf16 at every point where eager HF rounds reproduces native L0.m to 0.03 spacings, 99.4 percent of elements bit-equal. fp32 fails the current rule too (L0.m 41.6 spacings vs 12.4, L1.m 85 vs 18). The reduced-precision flag changes nothing at batch 1 (bitwise). A worst-case propagated bound is not finite from L0.p on.

resolution: Closed in 5282709. The float64 chain was correct; the 0.378 at t21.L0.m is the rounding effect of bf16 attention scores (|s| about 1.5e4, spacing 64: rounding ties the top scores, so the native softmax is not the softmax of the real scores). A forecast now seals two predictions: exact (float64, the math) and emulated (the same identities run with the backend's own kernels in the model dtype at the native batch-1 shapes, rounding where eager HF rounds; derived-exact under stated premises). `verify` decides against the emulated one with a floor of 1 spacing (supplied; measured maximum 0). MEASURED job-c5130b0aaf7e, Qwen2.5-1.5B, RTX 4080, torch 2.13.0+cu130: emulated is bit-equal to native at every stop, bf16 28 layers and fp32 2-layer cut, 3 prompts, sealed at L0.h and L14.h, where exact is 35-78 spacings off at L0.m; 48 seal/verify pairs through mdb all confirmed at 0 spacings. A float64 chain rounded once per sum is NOT enough (0-8 spacings off in bf16, 1-35 in fp32). Above the floor the verdict is `not confirmed` (a stage's native value outside its identity's bound, stage named) or `unresolved` (rounding drift, parting stop and ties named). `rounding_effect` = native - exact and the sealed `rounding_origin` are reported. detail: The same edit on the same prompt gives two different `derived-exact` predictions depending on where the cursor is. `whatif L20.m = clean:L20.m --consumer M[hot,cold]`: at t21.logits (mode rewind) exact dM = 0.59034, linear 0.49743, nonlinear 0.092911, residual 0.035; at t21.L0.h (mode ahead) exact dM = 0.50414, linear 0.49671, nonlinear 0.007424, residual 0.121. Native dM is 0.625 both times. Two values carrying the label derived-exact for one quantity differ by 0.086 (more than the residual either reports). Not known which is right: in mode ahead the operands downstream of the cursor are not measured yet, so the chain may be using forecast operands or a truncated nonlinear term while still labelled exact.
evidence: job-59cba8de26fc and job-176bc5bdcee7 (Qwen2.5-1.5B bf16 cuda); logs in packages/mdb/results/engine-r6-20261113/
next: Find what each mode uses as operands for the exact chain. If mode ahead predicts from forecast operands, the label must say so (derived from sealed forecasts, with their residual), or the exact chain must be completed after the native run measures the operands; the two modes must agree to rounding on the tiny models and that must be a test.
resolution: Closed in 0d93b30. Cause (measured on tiny bf16): rewind mode used the native base consumer, so exact = F(x1) - y0_native folded the base run's own rounding eta0 into exact and nonlinear (eta0 3.6e-4 matched the gap exactly); a no-op edit had exact -0.00037 instead of 0. Both chains now compute F(x1) - F(x0) on the same operands with the port at x0. With the consumer ahead, the sealed value is marked as built on operands forecast from the cursor; after the native run exact is recomputed on measured operands (report.exact, split term `operands`) and the verdict uses it, so the verdict is the same at any cursor. detail: On Qwen2.5-1.5B bf16 cuda the forecast and whatif chain rounding bounds do not resolve: forecast M and L26.m sealed at L0 or L24 print `bound unresolved (the propagated bound is not finite: the operands' bounds are too wide for this identity)`, and a whatif from L24 printed a rounding-effect bound of 1.6325e+36 [bound]. Independent of the accumulation premise: same result with allow_bf16_reduced_precision_reduction = False (fp32 premise, gamma about 1e-4). Not traced which identity blows up; suspected the large attention scores (L0 |s| about 1.5e4) or RMSNorm of large activations in the interval propagation. Cause measured (job-6d8b03288147, source 20edd23): no threshold is involved. The chain bound assumes every rounding error aligns; the score interval is 12.9 at L24 (measured error 0.069) and 1346 at L0 (measured 67.9), softmax worst case multiplies by exp(2*interval) (1.7e11, then float64 overflow to inf/nan), and RMSNorm plus the SwiGLU product square it per layer. The forecast itself is exact: emulated equals native at every stage. Per-stage bounds on native operands hold at 532/533 stages; the one miss is L0.p, where fp32 exp underflows to 0 and the softmax bound has no absolute term (asserted, reproduced on synthetic scores). Reporting makes an accurate forecast read as failed: seal prints `state: unresolved`, names the consumer rather than the stage that broke, omits the emulated prediction; whatif prints `within bound 1.6e36`.

See M62 for the cost of stage checks.

detail: forecast.seal refuses while a staged edit sits between the cursor and the target, so sealing the exact chain of a cell-edit arm needs the cursor stepped past the edited layer first (exp1: set_cell at t<last>.L20.h, until t<last>.L21.h, seal M, until logits, verify: ~3 s per arm, verdict 'confirmed' on the smoke items). A 'seal including staged edits' mode would let the forecast cover the edit's own layer.
resolution: Fixed (93f28f4). Measured first: a staged set_cell never refused a seal (the chain reads read_cache(staged=True)); only staged port edits (run.set) did, so exp1's step to L21 was unnecessary. forecast.seal(staged='include') builds the staged port edits of the pending layer into both the exact and the emulated chain (propagate's M55 edit functions), so a forecast sealed before the edited layer covers the edit's own layer; the record carries a 'staged' block (mode, edits, sha256) only in include mode or when something is staged (legacy bytes unchanged); verify decides targets the included edit wrote (staged_included). Measured on 8 tiny configs: v/r/m/s port edits and a cell edit at L1 sealed at or before L1.h verify 'confirmed' (residual 0 spacings). Default still refuses. The REPL forecast verb does not expose the mode yet. Exp1's 26/26 stays a fidelity check (audit correction 2).

Binding.component needs the residual t<r>.L<l>.h of the carrier row, so the run must step that row (prefill <= r); captures that keep only K/V (twohop-run1 1a/1c) cannot feed it, contrary to the memo's 'offline from the 1a captures'. cell_sweep then needs a second, unedited run at the pending row. A capture option saving h at declared rows would make the component table offline.
resolution: Fixed for the binding (ee90c0e). components.ResidualCapture.from_run(run, rows, layers) saves h at declared rows plus the V cache (save/load); component_binding(None, ..., capture=cap, adapter=...) builds the binding with no forward; provenance records where h and the native cell came from. Measured on tiny Qwen2 bf16 / Qwen3 fp32: offline binding bitwise equal to live (components, native, linear, rho), incl. after a disk round trip. K/V-only captures are refused (h not recoverable). component_table still needs a live run (attention mix, readout).

detail: Showcase exp6: of mdb's above-floor (2 bf16 spacings) patch effects, 60/274 (Qwen3-0.6B-Base) and 16/228 (Qwen2.5-0.5B) flip or fall below the floor when the same forward is run batched through the unprocessed TL bridge (kernel path only, no reparametrisation); processing adds 46/257 and 82/249. resolution: Fixed (93f28f4), reframed per AUDIT-SHOWCASE.md: the 2-spacing floor stays the noise bound; new mdb.analysis.stability adds a 'kernel-sensitive' band for |effect| <= k floors (default STABLE_FLOORS=4, supplied from exp6: 0/214 losses above 4 floors) and calibrate() measures k per model from paired effects of two realisations (loss table by bin, sign reversals, JSON Calibration). supplied.judge and forecast.verify take kernel_path/calibration/stable_floors and add 'stability', 'kernel_path' (default 'mdb-stepped'), k and floors; existing verdict fields unchanged. Measured on exp6 outputs (reproduces the audit bins; results/showcase-20261114/sc-fixes/calib-*.json): kernel path only k=2.125 (Qwen3-0.6B-Base, 60/274 lost) and 2.0 (Qwen2.5-0.5B, 16/228); all paths pooled k=2.125 and 3.75. Correction to this issue's text: losses are almost all fall-below-floor, not sign flips (1/274; 28/228 all from processing), and on Qwen2.5 processing (82/249) not kernel path dominates. The subspace interchange also reports effect in floors as a numeric column.
